caption.text: Hi, I'm Dana, and if you're new here, welcome. I've been a dietitian for 15 years and started Harborlight in 2013, but I didn't understand what a complex patient goes through until I became one. Swipe for the short version of how I work.

If you're new here, hi. We're Harborlight Nutrition & Integrative Wellness, a team of dietitians who work a little differently. We take the cases that don't fit in one box: gut, histamine, hormones, mold, pediatrics. Entirely virtual. Not sure who's the right fit? Book a call and we'll tell you.

Most people hear "dietitian" and think meal plans, calories, eat more vegetables. In complex cases food is rarely the whole story. We look at gut infections, mold, hormones, immune signals and nutrient status to find out why your body is reacting. If you feel like the complex case, you're not imagining it. DM us "I'm ready" when you want to find the root cause.

You come to me expecting another list of foods to avoid, and we end up talking about what we can add back. Expanding someone's food list is often the start of feeling better. If your list keeps shrinking and you still feel bad, book a free call through the link in bio.

Feeling rough and need something easy? This is the smoothie I recommend when you're bloated, puffy and tired: mango, ginger, a scoop of collagen, coconut water and a handful of greens. Save it. Recipe in the caption.

Your gut doesn't have to hurt to belong in your endometriosis assessment. When we work with endo and hormone concerns we look at how the liver, intestine and microbes handle estrogen. Our nutrition care works alongside your treatment. Book a call through the link in bio.

"Ok, but my body reacts to everything. Where do I even start?" So many of you asked after my last post. Here is the order I go in: calm things down before clearing anything out, make sure the exits are open, widen your food instead of shrinking it, one change at a time. Ready for a plan that fits your body? DM us READY and we'll reach out.

Your lymphatic system moves immune cells, fluid and waste, and it has no pump, so it depends on how you live. Walking, rebounding, sauna, diaphragmatic breathing, beets and greens, berries, citrus, ginger, hydration, dry brushing and regular bowel movements all help. DM us or comment if you'd like support.

The fall harvest salad I'm making on repeat: roasted sweet potato and beets, crisp apple, pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, shaved parmesan over massaged kale with an apple cider dressing. Serves 4. Add chicken or turkey for a full meal. Low-histamine swaps at the end.

Could mast-cell activation be connected to insulin resistance? Mast cells live in metabolic tissue too, and researchers are studying their role in inflammation and insulin signalling. Important distinction: a mechanism worth studying is not a clinically established relationship. We evaluate each carefully rather than assume.

You're not paying for another meal plan. The biggest misconception about working with a dietitian is that we only tell you what to eat. We read your history, symptoms, labs, medications and lifestyle, and the plan evolves as you do. This is what concierge integrative nutrition looks like. Visit the link in bio to inquire about becoming a patient.

I'm an integrative dietitian. Of course I ask about your bowel movements, want every lab from the last five years, and have seventeen follow-up questions before we get to food. After 13 years, the best clues come from the questions nobody asked. Fellow dietitians, what would you add?
